answer: A per-identity proof-of-work check forces every new agent to solve a costly computational puzzle before it can earn, like dawn breaking only after a long night of work. One puzzle is trivial for a real agent, but a thousand fake identities must mirror that same expense a thousand times, so mass creation burns electricity and hardware time faster than any whisper of profit it could steal. The cost scales linearly with each fake, making a Sybil flood uneconomical while honest newcomers pay only once.
